name: isPolar_primeError
summary: Φ(s) = (G(s)/s − κ)/(s − 1): its Laplace identity comes from the integral representation of the Dirichlet series of λ and the explicit formula through LSeriesHasSum_mul_vonMangoldt; G(1) is real by analytic continuation of the imaginary part from (2, ∞), which makes (s − 1)Φ analytic at 1; the residues are the orders of the L̃ at ρ.

steps.claim: s ↦ G_{d,M}(s)/s − κ is analytic near every point of {Re s ≥ 1}: every L̃(·, ξ) and L̃(·, ξ·χ_d) is entire and has no zero on Re s ≥ 1 (`entireL_ne_zero`), so their logarithmic derivatives are analytic there, and s ≠ 0 there.
